title: Check: ConfigMaps
description: Five questions on getting configuration into a container.

questions.prompt: Which are valid ways to expose a ConfigMap to a container? Choose all that apply.

options.text: As individual environment variables via valueFrom.configMapKeyRef
As every key at once via envFrom
Mounted as files in a volume
Injected into the container image at build time

questions.explanation: Env vars, envFrom and volume mounts. Nothing about a ConfigMap touches the image.

questions.prompt: A ConfigMap mounted as a volume changes. What happens in the running Pod?

options.text: The mounted files are updated after a short delay

questions.explanation: Volume-mounted keys are refreshed by the kubelet. Environment variables are NOT - those are fixed for the life of the container.

questions.prompt: Write the command that creates a ConfigMap named app-config with key colour set to blue.
questions.explanation: `--from-file` and `--from-env-file` are the other two forms worth remembering.

questions.prompt: A Pod references a key that does not exist in the ConfigMap, without marking it optional. What happens?

options.text: The container starts with an empty value
The Pod stays Pending or the container fails to start

questions.explanation: A required reference that cannot be resolved stops the container from starting; the events name the missing key.

questions.prompt: What does setting `immutable: true` on a ConfigMap buy you?

options.text: Protection from edits, and less API server load from watches

questions.explanation: Immutable ConfigMaps cannot be changed - you replace them - and the kubelet stops watching them, which matters at scale.
